content_html:
If you are planning a trip to Cusco, it is important to know that the rainy season goes from November to March, with its highest point in January and February. Although many travelers prefer the dry season (May to October), visiting Cusco during the rainy season It also has advantages and it can be a great experience if you prepare properly.

Advantages of traveling to Cusco in the rainy season

Fewer tourists and better prices

If you want to avoid the crowds in places like Machu Picchu, the Sacred Valley or Sacsayhuamán, this is an excellent opportunity. Furthermore, the prices of accommodation, tours and train tickets They are usually lower.

Greener and more vibrant landscapes

The rains make the landscapes look spectacular. The valleys and mountains will be covered in intense green, which will make your photos incredible.

Milder climate

Unlike the dry season, when temperatures can drop to 0°C at night, in the rainy season the climate is more warm, with minimums of 7-10°C in the city of Cusco.

Disadvantages and precautions

Unpredictable rains

Downpours can fall at any time of the day, although they are usually more intense in the afternoons. Always carry a rain poncho and waterproof shoes so as not to ruin your adventure.

Slippery roads and possible landslides

If you plan to go hiking (such as the Inca Trail or the Mountain of 7 Colors), Please note that paths may be slippery or even closed for security. Check with travel agencies before booking.

Changes in transportation

Rains may affect flights and trains to Machu Picchu. Always check the schedules and consider purchasing flexible tickets in case there are delays or cancellations.
